title: Visits to Every Subdomain

concept.title: One record adds to several keys
body: A visit to `discuss.leetcode.com` is also a visit to `leetcode.com` and to `com`. So one input record has to be added to **several keys** of the map: the whole domain and each of its endings that start after a dot.

body.code:
parts = domain.split(".")
for i in range(len(parts)):
    sub = ".".join(parts[i:])
    visits[sub] = visits.get(sub, 0) + count

body: The map accumulates the sum of the visit counts for each key. In the end, sort the keys to print them in a fixed order; a map never promises any order by itself.

statement: You get `n` records. Each record has a number of visits and a domain such as `discuss.leetcode.com`. A visit to a domain is also a visit to each of its parent domains: `discuss.leetcode.com`, `leetcode.com` and `com`. Compute the total number of visits for every domain and parent domain that occurs. Print how many different domains there are, and then one line per domain with its total visits and its name, in alphabetical order of the names.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has the number of visits and the domain, separated by a space.
outputFormat: The first line: the number of different domains.
Then one line per domain: `visits name`.
constraints: A domain has 1 to 4 parts separated by dots; each part has 1 to 6 lowercase letters.

examples.note: com gets 950, google.mail.com 900, mail.com 900 and yahoo.com 50.

hints: A record with the domain `a.b.c` adds its visits to `a.b.c`, `b.c` and `c`.
Use a map from the domain name to the total visits.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
e = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: Each record adds its visits to its domain and to every parent domain (the text after each dot). The map is printed in sorted order of the names.
solution.complexity: Time O(total length * parts), space O(total length).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
e = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

visits = {}
for cnt, domain in e:
    c = int(cnt)
    parts = domain.split(".")
    for i in range(len(parts)):
        sub = ".".join(parts[i:])
        visits[sub] = visits.get(sub, 0) + c
print(len(visits))
for sub in sorted(visits):
    print(visits[sub], sub)
